verdict: AMD's record $13.4B quarter was powered by its data-center business nearly doubling — the AI boom finally has a second chip supplier at scale.

segments.name: Data Center
segments.note: Instinct AI accelerators and EPYC server processors — a record quarter as AI builders bought GPUs and CPUs together.

segments.name: Client and Gaming
segments.note: PC chips (Ryzen) grew 7% to $2,949M, but gaming revenue fell 40% to $773M on weaker console and graphics demand.

segments.name: Embedded
segments.note: Chips designed into aircraft, cars, telecom gear and factory equipment — steady, long-cycle business.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Designing AI accelerators, processors and the software around them.

opex.name: Marketing, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling chips and running the company.

opex.name: Amortization of acquisition intangibles
opex.note: Writing down technology and brands bought in past deals (mainly Xilinx) — bookkeeping, not cash. Another $257M of it sits in cost of sales.

takeaways.title: Data Center is the company now
takeaways.text: $8.5B of the $13.4B total, on record Instinct GPU and EPYC CPU sales; management expects growth to accelerate as Helios systems ramp.

takeaways.title: Two versions of profit
takeaways.text: Non-GAAP EPS was $2.09; GAAP EPS was $1.46. Almost the whole gap is the non-cash warrant charge described below.

takeaways.title: Gaming is the weak spot
takeaways.text: Gaming revenue fell 40% to $773M — console chips and graphics cards are shrinking while everything AI-adjacent booms.

oneTimers: The $1,097M warrant charge is non-cash: AMD granted two large customers warrants for up to 160M shares each (at $0.01) tied to purchase milestones; as AMD's share price climbed, the accounting value of that promise jumped, and the increase is booked as a loss. It will keep swinging with the share price until the warrants vest.
Income tax was a $555M benefit this quarter instead of the usual expense, which also lifted GAAP net income; AMD's non-GAAP results use a normalized 13% tax rate.
otherDetail: A $1,097M paper loss on stock warrants granted to two big AI customers — the promised shares are worth more because AMD's share price rose — plus $62M of interest expense, partly offset by $123M of interest income, $67M of investment gains and $5M of equity income: a net $959M cost. Taxes, unusually, added a $555M benefit rather than a bill.
follow100Note: The tax line is a benefit (money back), so it adds instead of subtracting; the rows reconcile to $100 within a cent of rounding.
footerNote: Other income (expense), net and its warrant charge are detailed in AMD's Q3 2026 Form 10-Q; headline figures are from the earnings release.
